questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to save money when shopping online at night
Why celebrities earn so much from TV adverts
How behavioural science influences what we do
Why many fast-food restaurants are now closing
questions.why: They look at the ways people can be convinced to do things, using ideas from behavioural science.

questions.q: Why did Pippa buy new headphones?
options: Her old ones broke, so she researched carefully
A famous celebrity recommended them online
They were on special offer in a local shop
A friend who works in music gave her advice
questions.why: She says her old ones broke and she did lots of research to find a good pair.

questions.q: Why does Phil think he bought a soft drink that morning?
options: It was the cheapest drink in the shop
He was very thirsty after a long run
A friendly shop worker suggested it to him
Someone he likes may have advertised it
questions.why: Phil says it might be because he saw someone he likes promoting it in an advert.

questions.q: According to Ben Jones, why do endorsements work?
options: Because the products really are always better
When unsure, we follow people we see as experts
Because the adverts are repeated many times a day
Because famous people are paid a lot to say it
questions.why: He says when we're unsure, it's easy to follow the lead of those we think are credible.

questions.q: Why does Ben mention parents and teachers?
options: To say they often give bad advice about shopping
To explain that children see too many adverts
To show we learn early to trust people who know
To suggest teachers should promote more products
questions.why: He says we start following credible people early, like parents and teachers who help us learn.

questions.q: According to Dean Ward, why do people spend more at touchscreen machines?
options: The food is cheaper when ordered on the screen
They don't feel judged and have more time
The machines only show the large portions
Staff are not allowed to help them order
questions.why: He says people don't feel judged by a screen and have more time, so they say yes to extras.

questions.q: How much more do people usually spend when using the touchscreens?
options: About 5%
About 50%
About double
About 25–30%
questions.why: Dean says they typically see an increased basket spend of 25–30%.

questions.q: Why did the World Food Programme in Tunisia make a TV series?
options: To get people to eat together by copying others
To sell more restaurant meals to young families
To teach people how to cook cheap, healthy food
To advertise healthy snacks to schoolchildren
questions.why: They wanted people to eat together more, as people learn by imitating and observing others.
